stories.title: Flintshire meets recycling target but £1m fine still looms
stories.summary: Flintshire County Council still has a Welsh Government fine of more than £1 million hanging over it for missing a statutory recycling target. That is despite the authority successfully transforming its waste collection services to hit the necessary 70% household rubbish recycling rate over the last 18 months. stories.summary: Work has started on bringing a former industrial site at the Port of Mostyn back into use, as part of a £14.7 million upgrade backed by the North Wales Growth Deal. stories.title: Welsh Water emergency work leaves villages near Holywell with low or no water
stories.summary: Homes in villages south of Holywell may have no water or low water pressure this morning because of emergency work by Welsh Water. The area affected, shown on Welsh Water’s map, runs from Pantasaph and Brynford, alongside the A55, down through Pentre Halkyn, Halkyn and The Catch to Pen-y-parc near Rhosesmor. stories.summary: A Welsh Government Minister has heard first-hand how transport costs and limited bus services are affecting young people’s access to education, as Coleg Cambria renewed calls for fairer funding across Wales. stories.title: Flintshire drug deaths stay at highest level in more than a decade as health board says trend is a concern
stories.summary: Seventeen drug poisoning deaths were registered in Flintshire last year, the same as in 2024 and up from five in 2022, official figures show.
